title: ASRock Rack W890D8-2L2T Review Intel Xeon 600 Server and Workstation Platform
gist: ASRock Rack's W890D8-2L2T motherboard puts Intel's workstation-class Xeon 600 series into a CEB-like board built to double as a rack-mounted server, reflecting a broader shift of high-core-count workstation platforms into datacenter GPU-hosting duty.

insights.claim: Workstation-class platforms built around high-core-count Xeon CPUs with eight memory channels are increasingly being deployed in rack-mounted form to host GPUs and accelerators, blurring the line between workstation and server categories.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Watch motherboard/OEM vendors (ASRock Rack, Supermicro, Gigabyte) expanding workstation-socket boards into rackmount SKUs as a low-cost on-ramp for GPU-hosting capacity outside hyperscaler datacenters.
insights.quote: That latter category is becoming more exciting. Beyond the appeal of having relatively high-core-count Xeon CPUs with eight memory channels in a workstation, many are using this type of platform to host GPUs and accelerators.
insights.locator: intro paragraph, 'The ASRock Rack W890D8-2L2T is a really interesting motherboard'

insights.claim: The ASRock Rack W890D8-2L2T motherboard uses a CEB-like 12-inch by 10.9-inch form factor, larger than standard ATX, because the Intel LGA4710-2 socket and its eight-DIMM DDR5 array require the extra board space.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: System integrators need non-standard cases/mounting for this class of board, a minor but real friction point for whitebox rackmount workstation builds.

insights.claim: The board provides seven PCIe Gen5 x16 slots that can alternatively run as CXL 2.0 x16 links, giving the platform native CXL memory/accelerator expansion capability at the motherboard level.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Broad CXL 2.0 support on a mainstream workstation-server board signals CXL is moving from niche hyperscaler use into mainstream Xeon platforms, a leading indicator for CXL memory-pooling product adoption.
insights.quote: There are seven PCIe Gen5 x16 slots that can also be CXL 2.0 x16.

insights.claim: The board also includes two MCIO x8 connectors and an additional MCIO x4 connector, all running PCIe Gen5/CXL 2.0 or configurable as SATA, adding further high-speed expansion beyond the seven full-length slots.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Dense onboard PCIe Gen5/CXL connectivity reduces the need for external switches in small accelerator or NVMe-heavy deployments, a cost lever for budget-constrained AI/edge builds.

insights.claim: The platform requires four separate 8-pin CPU power inputs, an unusually high count that the reviewer flags as a power-supply compatibility consideration for builders.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Signals rising per-socket power delivery requirements for workstation-class Xeons, consistent with the broader trend of higher TDP CPUs straining standard PSU/power-connector ecosystems.
insights.quote: There are a total of four 8-pin power inputs, so make sure your power supply is up to the task of powering this, as finding that many CPU power inputs is not easy.

insights.claim: ASRock Rack chose Intel's own E610 dual 10GbE NIC for the primary onboard networking, paired with Intel i210 1GbE ports, keeping the board's core networking silicon entirely within Intel's own component stack.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Shows Intel using its own NIC silicon (E610) to capture networking attach-rate on its own Xeon boards rather than ceding that slot to Broadcom/Marvell/Realtek, a small but relevant data point on Intel's networking silicon push.
insights.locator: Intel E610 dual 10GbE NIC heatsink paragraph

insights.claim: Out-of-band management on the board runs through an ASPEED AST2600 BMC exposing IPMI and VGA, continuing ASPEED's default incumbency as the baseboard management controller of choice on server-class motherboards.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Reinforces ASPEED's near-monopoly position in the BMC market even as boards diversify elsewhere, relevant to anyone tracking ASPEED's server-attach exposure.
